clauses.text:
JErecuthve Orber
Mr. Edward Rappholt may be reinstated to the position of letter
carrier in the post office at New York City without regard to the length
of his separation from the service.
Mr. Rappholt was appointed as substitute letter carrier at St. Louis,
Missouri, January2,190o; transferred to New Fork City post office
August 10, 19o8; to the Atlanta, Georgia, post office October 16, 1912;
mnd resigned December S, 112 He made application for reinstatement
ii December, 1913. His application for reinstatement wvas referred to the
postmaster at New York City, March I I, 1914, and disapproved.
Tbis order is issued upon the recommendation of the Acting Post-
man *r General, in view of the fact that Mr. Rappholt's record as a letter
carrier was good, and that the failure to approve his request for reinstate-
nment in the New York City post office at a time when it could have been
made in accordance with the civil service rules, was due to a local rule
rather than to a Departmental rule or policy.
The Civil Service Commission does not concur in the recommendation.
WOODROW WILSON
THE WH~ITIE HOUSE,
23 February, 1916.
No. 2'27-1
